items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: The interviewee discusses George Meany's political and labor union stance ('represent the working class of America', 'alliance with the capitalists') but provides no evidence of a personal, professional, or musical connection.

ctx.x: I just wonder, when you use the classic motto of capitalist labor, how you apply that to the American context, where you have a union, unionization of labor, which is so strong and conservative. It seems to me if the American people are going to be done in by anything, it's going to be George Meany as much as it is anybody else, and he represents the working class of America.

Well, as long as he continues to represent the working class of America, then the nation will not succumb to George Meany. The danger lies in that point where he decides for his own interest to make an alliance with the capitalists, that the danger exists.
Which has been done since the real history of American labor.
